findings.evidence: Substitute your own directory for `build/` in both that line and the verification command below.
findings.note: Step 1 is written as a concrete command to execute (`echo 'build/' >> .gitignore`) and only afterward, in step 2, does the text say to substitute the real directory name, so a literal executor may append the placeholder 'build/' before realizing it needed to swap it out first.

findings.evidence: The working directory is the repository root, so `.gitignore` and the path being ignored are both relative to it.
findings.note: The stated preconditions (repo-root cwd, git on PATH, directory untracked) cover everything the procedure and verification actually rely on.

findings.evidence: Run before step 1 it exits 1; run after step 1 it exits 0, on the same working tree.
findings.note: git check-ignore -q genuinely flips from exit 1 to exit 0 once the pattern is added, so the verification would correctly fail if the procedure were skipped.
